owner: constraint-layered layout and agent quality oracle
problem: A zero-indegree source that serves a local row and consumers four or more visual rows away can retain a long vertical trunk, while the existing partition solver arbitrarily caps the rendering at two anchors.
scope: Geometry-derived rendering aliases for any zero-indegree component and agent-only route statistics; logical topology, component identity, public JSON and CLI remain unchanged.
baseline: The local-plus-four-row case is eligible, but four independently separated consumer bands collapse to two anchors; per-edge reports also omit full route length and bend attribution.
benchmarks: yFiles hierarchical edge grouping and bus-style routing
ELK edge sections and exact port-based layered routing
one-dimensional uncapacitated facility location with fixed opening cost
graph-drawing vertex splitting with a penalty on split count
advantages: Existing aliases preserve one logical source and exact library geometry
Existing acceptance checks already reject topology, obstacle, overlap, crossing and bend regressions
disadvantages: Two-anchor cap is not general for three or more separated consumer bands
Area is currently treated as a hard veto even though it is lower priority than route readability
Routing statistics do not yet attribute full length and bends to each edge and logical source
limitations: Rendering aliases are allowed only for zero-indegree logical vertices
Exact global minimization of crossings, bends and rectilinear net length is computationally hard
The layout remains deterministic and must stay practical for 4096-clock stress inputs
defects: Known failure fixture with four separated bands returns only two anchors
A lower-priority area increase can block a route-length or crossing improvement
Final report cannot yet identify the full route length and bend count of an individual edge
bottlenecks: Facility partition cost can become quadratic in the number of distinct consumer axes
Independent quality recomputation must not share production-only cached values

metrics.name: avoidable long source trunks
metrics.measurement: independent geometry-derived facility partition compared with rendered anchor assignments
metrics.evidence: focused source-replication tests and layout_quality report

metrics.name: route length attribution
metrics.measurement: sum Manhattan length of canonical final edge segments

metrics.name: crossing attribution
metrics.measurement: orthogonal sweep over canonical final edge segments

metrics.name: logical topology preservation
metrics.unit: missing, extra or duplicate logical edges
metrics.measurement: compare source/target logical names and exact named ports
metrics.evidence: replica identity and edge fault-injection tests

hypotheses: Removing the arbitrary two-anchor cap lets the fixed-cost facility objective choose every justified consumer band without fixture-specific rules
Modeling one shared trunk by its covered span rather than a sum of per-consumer L1 distances prevents fan-out count from causing excessive aliases
Treating area as a tie-break rather than a hard veto prevents compactness from defeating readability
Per-edge canonical segment statistics provide sufficient attribution for regression diagnosis
allowed_variables: facility partition count selected by geometry
source replica acceptance objective after hard gates

stages.input: known good, known bad and neighboring source layouts
stages.checker: pytest focused source partition and quality tests
stages.rollback: retain the failing fixture and revert only new oracle code

stages.input: sorted target port axes and geometry-derived row pitch
stages.rollback: restore previous solver while keeping the failure fixture

stages.input: logical DAG, supplied library geometry and partition result
stages.output: one logical root with one or more rendering anchors
stages.rollback: reject the candidate and retain the prior valid layout

stages.input: complete examples, stress corpus and release bundle
stages.rollback: do not commit, push or release

hard_gates: Only zero-indegree logical vertices may have rendering aliases
Every logical edge appears exactly once with exact ports
No node, label, edge-node or different-net-overlap regression
Crossings and bends cannot worsen when accepting aliases
Known failure rejection and known success acceptance are both 100 percent
4096-clock stress runtime remains within the project budget
failure_fixtures: one local consumer plus one consumer four rows away but one long source trunk
four separated bands arbitrarily reduced to two anchors
replica attached to an intermediate node
same-net crossing miscounted as a different-net crossing
success_fixtures: one local consumer plus one four rows away uses two anchors
near consumers within three rows retain one shared trunk
contiguous many-row fanout retains a justified shared trunk
three or more independently separated bands use the facility-optimal anchor count
renamed and reordered equivalent graphs produce equivalent metrics
fault_injections: change a replica logical_name to a non-root
add a redundant adjacent source replica
inject one orthogonal crossing and require exact edge/source attribution
rollback: Candidate aliases are never applied unless all hard geometry and topology gates pass; repository changes are not uploaded until the full delivery gate passes.

iteration_budget.review_trigger: a second failure must change the model, measurement or owner rather than tune a fixture threshold

stop_conditions: All frozen success and failure fixtures produce the expected decision
Production and independent route statistics are equal
Focused, full, frozen-source and packaged gates pass

promotion_decision.reason: The capability is project-domain-specific and already has a stable project skill owner.

writeback: Update project clock-layout and diagram-design references; add the general cross-project rule to the user-root clock-tree-layout reference only after the implementation and regression evidence pass.
